feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
This is a strong, credible CV with clear senior-level progression, relevant digital strategy expertise, and good evidence of scope across web, content, analytics, and multimedia. It reads professionally and is mostly polished, but it would be stronger with tighter structure, more quantified outcomes, and a few wording/consistency fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, culminating in director-level leadership and now consulting; this supports credibility and growth.  
- Strong breadth of expertise across digital strategy, Drupal/CMS, analytics, governance, email, social, and multimedia, aligned to the target title.  
- Good use of scale indicators such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers,” which adds impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond scope: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, email performance, production efficiencies, cost savings, or campaign results.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; the CV currently feels repetitive and slightly overlong.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; maintain consistent comma usage in lists (“workflows and systems” vs. “workflows, systems”); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning).” No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s recent leadership roles. It would be sharper with a more specific opening, cleaner grammar, and a bit more emphasis on senior-level outcomes over broad capability lists.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” and tighten phrasing for a more polished, executive tone.
- Lead with current positioning: “Digital communications and strategy leader” to match the subtitle and recent director/consulting experience.
- Replace generic lists with higher-value themes such as enterprise web strategy, digital operations, governance, and mission-driven audience engagement.
- Consider a rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and digital operations for complex, mission-driven organizations. Strong track record in advocacy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and “stakeholder coordination” are repeated in Core Competencies/Soft Skills.
- “Platform modernization” and workflow/systems language also recur in Topline Skills and recent experience.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it sharper and less repetitive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and standardize style: “Multi-channel communications” instead of “communication.”
- Replace generic items with more distinctive strengths tied to recent roles, e.g.: “Digital strategy & platform modernization • Editorial systems & governance • Web/CMS administration • Analytics & performance reporting • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production”
- Consider swapping “Workflow & systems architecture” for “Content operations & workflow design” if you want clearer, less technical wording.
- Order by strategic relevance first, then executional skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header; consider removing here.
- “Multi-channel communications” and analytics/workflow themes already appear in Topline Skills, so this section should stay concise and high-level.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the prior NACo positions and Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level scope, strategic outcomes, and only the newest work not already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancement, and cross-channel communications operations as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-led bullets; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one line focused on organization-wide coordination.
- Rephrase technical bullet for outcome: “Built Drupal campaign experiences and reusable microsite/toolkit components to improve speed, consistency, and member access to resources.”
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/components launched, workflow time reduced, search accuracy gains, engagement lift, or stakeholder teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search,” microsites, and campaign storytelling duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold the detail.
- Governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement also echo the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize external advisory scope and post-director contributions.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget management for a national membership organization.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into 4–5 bullets, prioritizing measurable impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-focused: add newsletter list size, engagement growth, campaign performance, or production volume if available; otherwise trim vague phrasing like “serving thousands of followers.”
- Strengthen results language: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal production capacity for advocacy programming, events and recurring video series”; “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery reporting to improve executive visibility and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version higher-level and more strategic.
- Video-programming language also echoes older NACo entries; focus here on building the studio and scaling capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level, with tighter phrasing and clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, supporting advocacy campaigns and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: managed 4 weekly newsletters; launched/scaled weekly advocacy video update; coordinated editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Replace soft phrasing like “helped improve” and “helping scale” with stronger verbs: “standardized,” “streamlined,” “expanded,” “institutionalized.”
- Add metrics if available: newsletter open/click rates, video cadence/views, publishing turnaround time, stakeholder/team count, or growth in audience/reach.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video” and “weekly updates” also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.
- “Governance/workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with the 2022–2024 role; keep this version tactical and execution-focused.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, higher-signal wording tied to recent scope:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Audience-centered content strategy for advocacy and member engagement
- Consider dropping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” if you want this section to emphasize systems/leadership over communications copywriting.
- Keep wording parallel and specific; avoid vague labels like “content planning” without “strategy” or “operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also overlaps with Core Competencies; rephrase to add scope or channel detail.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize highest-value, recent strengths tied to enterprise web modernization and delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from platform inventory to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization” is stronger than listing multiple CMSs first.
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths; move older/basic items like jQuery later or remove.
- Tighten to 6–8 items max, e.g.:
- Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization
- Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript)
- API integrations and workflow automation
- Airtable-based content and operational systems
- SharePoint and Power Pages
- AI-enabled search and discovery experiences
- If possible, align wording to proven outcomes elsewhere: “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “AI-enabled legislative search,” “systems supporting 50+ publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current list duplicates the detailed “Technical + IT” section almost line for line.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlaps with Core Competencies; keep wording distinct or more execution-focused.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Use a tighter mix of platforms and business-facing skills: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding • SEO and performance analysis”
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding” or “Decision-ready reporting” for stronger phrasing.
- If space allows, add one impact-oriented term such as “insight generation” or “conversion/performance optimization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current item duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section in Technical + IT almost exactly.
- Avoid listing every tool here if they already appear elsewhere; keep Topline Skills more strategic and summary-level.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior, recent digital-platform leader, this item should signal depth or be trimmed to avoid repeating stronger skills elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **CMS & Web Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, prioritize recency/strength by ordering as: **Drupal • SharePoint • Power Pages • WordPress • GitHub Pages**
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless you’ve used it meaningfully in recent work; it reads lighter than the rest.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep the stronger version in one place and make this one more concise.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t repeat that phrase here unless you add a specific differentiator.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw languages to capability-based phrasing: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping versioned basics (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless needed for ATS; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner and more current.
- If accurate, add scope or outcome-oriented qualifiers: “API integrations for analytics, CMS, and campaign workflows” or “GitHub Actions for deployment and publishing automation.”
- Put the strongest, more current tools first: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, API integrations, then front-end languages.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- Google Tag Manager may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” to reduce scatter.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and signal how these tools were used in recent leadership roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Group by function for faster scanning: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Slack • Microsoft Teams
- If accurate, add light context instead of a pure list: “Used to build content operations, cross-team planning workflows, and lightweight automations for web, editorial, and communications teams.”
- Prioritize strongest/recent tools; cut weaker or older ones if not central. Consider dropping Basecamp or Trello if usage was limited.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same language elsewhere.
- Slack/Teams are basic collaboration tools; keep only if they support a broader workflow-systems framing.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations, but it reads as a generic tool list. Strengthen it by signaling scale, platform ownership, or campaign/automation capability without repeating email achievements already covered in work experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename for clarity and breadth: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten product naming: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show depth, e.g. **campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Best rewrite: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “tens of thousands,” newsletter volume, or channel leadership here; those points are already stronger in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 roles.
- “Engagement” may overlap with broader communications claims elsewhere; “Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms” is more precise.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and the website refresh.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/timeline, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or engagement gains.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and supervised day-to-day work of a digital media associate.”
- If true, add one measurable management/process outcome: reduced turnaround time, increased publishing consistency, or expanded in-house production capacity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this as launching or establishing the format here.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats language used in later NACo entries; keep this version focused on foundational team setup.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Tighten it to emphasize innovation/program support plus the standout launch.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; developed digital and multimedia content to extend project visibility and member engagement.”
- Add the differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audience growth, stakeholder groups served, or how content supported policy/program goals.
- Remove vague phrasing like “contributed to” and “materials”; use stronger verbs such as “developed,” “produced,” or “launched.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing general digital content production, since later roles already cover web, video, newsletters and multimedia leadership in more depth.
- Don’t repeat “first in-house digital team” or weekly video/livestream themes from 2015–2024 roles.
